method: The two string forms escape different sets of characters. RFC 4515 defines a search filter assertion value over UTF-8 and requires the five octets NUL, left bracket, right bracket, asterisk and backslash to be written as a backslash and two hex digits, because a bare asterisk is a wildcard and a bare bracket would end the assertion; every escape in a filter value is that hex pair, so a backslash before an ordinary character is not valid there. RFC 4514 defines a distinguished-name value: a backslash is required before the quotation mark, plus, comma, semicolon, the two angle brackets and the backslash itself, before a number sign that starts the value, and before a space that starts or ends it; the equals sign and the slash need no escape. This page writes those three positional cases as hex pairs, uses the two-character form for the others, and writes filter hex in lower case and DN hex in upper case, which is how the RFC examples present them. Reading is byte-based: every hex pair becomes one octet, the raw characters contribute their UTF-8 bytes, and the whole sequence is decoded strictly, so an overlong form, a surrogate encoding, a truncated sequence or a stray octet above 0x7F is refused rather than replaced. A single-character backslash escape is accepted only in a DN value and only for the characters RFC 4514 lists. The optional non-ASCII switch writes each UTF-8 byte of an accented letter or emoji as a pair, which is valid in both forms and is what some older directory clients expect; left off, non-ASCII text stays as the RFC recommends for a valid UTF-8 string. The page escapes one attribute value, not a whole filter or DN: it does not build the surrounding assertion, split a multi-valued RDN or check whether an attribute name or OID is valid. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: RFC 4515 — LDAP: String Representation of Search Filters: the assertion value escapes for NUL, ( ) * and \, written as a backslash and two hex digits
RFC 4514 — LDAP: String Representation of Distinguished Names: escaping a leading # or space, a trailing space, the " + , ; < > \ characters and NUL
